entry.title: Re: [PATCH] platform/x86/intel/pmc: Add Sunrise Point-H support

div.pre:
Hi Angel,
Thanks for the patch, and for the detailed testing notes. The change looks reasonable to me. Without it, SPT-H systems fall into the Cannon Point path, and the debugfs output (e.g. ltr_show) is wrong. Your comparison against direct PWRMBASE reads is helpful.
A few comments: 1. Fixes tag: This adds support for a new device ID rather than fixing a regression introduced by 661405bd817b, so I'd drop the Fixes tag. It would also pull the patch into stable backports. 2. PFEAR map: As you note, spt_pfear_map is the SPT-LP layout and SPT-H has two more PCIe controllers (SPD/SPE). I couldn't find public documentation for the PCH-H PFEAR bits either, so I'm fine leaving the map as is. Please state in the commit message that the map is reused from SPT-LP and that SPD/SPE are not covered, so pch_ip_power_gating_status is incomplete for those controllers. If you can, a cross-check of PFEAR against the root ports present on your system would be useful, but it isn't required. A follow-up fixing the map is welcome once the bits can be confirmed.
With the Fixes tag dropped and the commit message updated, please send a v2. I'm happy to give a Reviewed-by after that. Thanks, Xi
On 10/5/2026 1:00 PM, Angel Lindo via B4 Relay wrote: > From: Angel Lindo <user5@example.test> > > spt_core_init() decides between the Sunrise Point and Cannon Point > register maps by looking for the Sunrise Point PMC PCI device, but only > the SPT-LP ID (0x9d21) is listed. On Skylake-H/Kaby Lake-H systems with > a Sunrise Point-H PCH (PMC 8086:a121), pci_dev_present() fails and the > driver takes the Coffee Lake path, using cnp_pmc_dev. That map does not > describe this PCH, so the debugfs output is wrong. > > Seen on a MacBookPro14,3 (i7-7820HQ, PCH-H, PMC 8086:a121). With the > stock driver, ltr_show lists Cannon Point IP names (SOUTHPORT_A, CNV, > EVA, ...) and every entry reads RAW 0xffffffff. I was debugging why > the package never goes deeper than PC3 on this machine, and without a > working PMC map there is no way to see which PCH IP blocks it. > > Add the SPT-H PMC ID to spt_pmc_pci_id[] so these systems use the > Sunrise Point map. > > Tested on MacBookPro14,3 (Apple firmware 529.140.2.0.0), kernel 7.2.5, > with the module built with this ID: > - ltr_show lists the Sunrise Point IP names, and the values match a > direct read of the PWRMBASE registers through /dev/mem bit for bit. > - pch_ip_power_gating_status follows device state: LPSS reads On while > the Bluetooth UART (00:1e.0) is bound and turns Off once it is > unbound and the UART enters D3hot. > - No warnings on load. > > Limitations: > - spt_pfear_map is the SPT-LP layout and is reused as is. SPT-H has > two more PCIe controllers (SPD and SPE). Bits 13 and 21 are RSVD in > the SPT map but SPD/SPE in the Cannon Point map; I could not verify > this on PCH-H, so the map is left unchanged. > - slp_s0_residency_usec reads 0 on this machine. > > Fixes: 661405bd817b ("platform/x86: intel_pmc_core: Special case for Coffeelake") > Assisted-by: claude-opus-5-5 > Signed-off-by: Angel Lindo <user5@example.test> > --- > On the same machine and firmware, macOS reaches PC10 (~81%) at idle, > while Linux never goes deeper than PC3. div.pre:

On Mon, 16 Nov 2026, Ilpo Järvinen wrote:
> On Mon, 16 Nov 2026, Magnus Lindholm wrote: > > On Mon, Nov 16, 2026 at 4:24 PM Ilpo Järvinen > > <user11@example.test> wrote: > > > > > > To serialize bridge window sizing and resource assignment, PCI core > > > needs to hold locks across both phases. Alpha nautilus PCI code calls > > > pci_bus_size_bridges() and pci_bus_assign_resources() separately > > > because it needs to do special resource alignment and setup after the > > > window sizes have been calculated. At least the former would seem to > > > belong to some existing __weak pcibios_*() hook but the latter might > > > need yet another pcibios_*() hook just for this single use. > > > > > > The nautilus code runs during init, so nothing is likely to race with > > > it. Converting it is mainly about consolidating the sizing and > > > assignment entry points of PCI core, which eventually allows removing > > > pci_bus_assign_resources(). > > > > > > Instead of trying to do a complex rework of the code, which is risky > > > without the ability to test on the hardware, simply convert > > > pci_bus_assign_resources() to pci_bus_size_and_assign_resources(). This > > > adds a small bit of extra work by performing the sizing step again, but > > > the calculations should yield the same sizes, so it seems safe > > > > > > > Agreed. By the second pass irongate_mem has been request_resource()d, so > > pbus_size_mem() skips it as assigned, and ioport_resource is never picked > > as a window (find_bus_resource_of_type()). Only the AGP bridge's > > unassigned windows are sized again, from the same inputs. > > > > That does rely on the assigned check, though: if your follow-up series > > starts sizing assigned windows, > > Yes, it will start to do that then. > > > nautilus' relocated root window > > (size_windows = 1) must stay untouched by the second pass. > > If the same size is calculated (during init, I see no reason why the > sizing results would change), there should be no change even when it > starts to assign windows. > > I'm bit worried though when it comes to the extra alignment done by this > nautilus code as that can change the size from the original but I don't > think there is anything that would allow shrinking the window even with > that so it looks okay to me even after the upcoming series. > > But it might be easiest to just set IORESOURCE_PCI_FIXED flag after the > resource has been added to the tree. That should keep the usual sizing > and assignment from touching it at all.
For the record, I realized this won't be necessary because nothing in the fitting and assignment algorithm can change the resource once it has been assigned.
All direct resource changes are (or should be) blocked for assigned resources to not corrupt the resource tree and root bus resources don't have bus->self so they never go into lists that need bus->self

entry.title: [PATCH net 7/7] mptcp: fix dummy mapping of overlapping segments

div.pre:
From: Geliang Tang <user34@example.test>
An MPTCP socket that has fallen back to TCP can silently lose received data if a segment partly overlaps data received earlier, and recv() then blocks, returning neither later data nor end of file.
After a fallback, subflow_check_data_avail() makes up a dummy mapping for the skb at the head of the subflow's receive queue, in which map_seq and map_subflow_seq must describe the same byte. But since commit 2834f8edd74d ("mptcp: cleanup fallback dummy mapping generation"), it computes map_seq from the first byte of the skb, while map_subflow_seq is still computed from copied_seq, the next unread byte. mptcp_subflow_get_mapped_dsn() then returns the data sequence number (DSN) of the first byte of the skb, instead of the one of copied_seq.
These two bytes differ for a segment that starts before rcv_nxt and ends after it, since TCP does not trim it. mptcp_init_skb() then gives the new bytes of this skb a DSN that is too low, and __mptcp_move_skb() skips some of them as old data, leaving a hole in the stream:
bytes 0 to 999 are received, the skb holds bytes 900 to 1499 byte 1000 gets the DSN of byte 900: too low by the 100 old bytes that is 100 below ack_seq, the next DSN that MPTCP expects __mptcp_move_skb() skips bytes 1000 to 1099 as old data ack_seq is the DSN of byte 1400, copied_seq is byte 1500 later data starts at the DSN of byte 1500: out of order the TCP FIN becomes a dummy DATA_FIN after the last byte ack_seq does not reach it, so there is no end of file
Fix this by computing map_subflow_seq from the first byte of the skb as well: mptcp_subflow_get_mapped_dsn() then returns the DSN of copied_seq.
Chris Mason sent the same fix in private, and found this issue with the help of an LLM. It has been reproduced in a VM, with the reproducer he shared, and with a new Packetdrill test: after a fallback to TCP, a segment overlapping data already received is injected. Without this patch, the new bytes at the beginning of this segment were lost, and the connection stalled, with no end of file:
reader 30.64: conn 1 BREAK: at my offset 1000 the bytes claim offset 1100: A GAP OF 100 BYTES reader 30.64: READ-TOTAL conn 1 outcome iii-gap-or-repeat bytes 1400 of 2500 [...] [...] end: hang: no data and no end of file for 30 s
And with the Packetdrill test:
dss_fallback_overlap_client.pkt:24: runtime error in read call: Expected result 2500 but got 1400 with errno 115 (Operation now in progress)
Fixes: 2834f8edd74d ("mptcp: cleanup fallback dummy mapping generation") Cc: user25@example.test Link: https://lore.kernel.org/user35@example.test [1] Co-developed-by: Chris Mason <user36@example.test> Signed-off-by: Chris Mason <user36@example.test> Signed-off-by: Geliang Tang <user34@example.test> [ Combine the commit messages of Geliang's [1] and Chris's versions. Commit message: how the issue was found, and its symptoms. ] Signed-off-by: Matthieu Baerts (NGI0) <user31@example.test> --- net/mptcp/subflow.c | 2 +- 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

entry.title: [PATCH net 6/7] mptcp: don't send a FIN before the pending data on fallback

div.pre:
When an MPTCP connection falls back to TCP after having been shut down, the data that is still in the write queue of the MPTCP socket is lost: a FIN is sent at fallback time, and this data cannot be sent after it. This can happen with TCP Fast Open (TFO), when a server writes data and shuts the connection down before the third ACK, and this ACK has no MPTCP options.
When the MPTCP socket has been shut down, mptcp_try_fallback() also shuts the subflow down: if the DATA_FIN had already been sent, nothing would send a FIN on this subflow otherwise. The commit introducing this only considered the case where all the data had already been pushed to the subflow.
The fix used here is to only shut the subflow down at fallback time if no new data is pending, i.e. if all the data before the DATA_FIN has already been sent. Otherwise, mptcp_check_send_data_fin() will do it once this data has been pushed, e.g. by the previous commit. Pending data that has been reinjected, e.g. after the failure of another subflow, is not new: it is already in this subflow.
This issue has been found by an AI code review agent, while reviewing the code of the previous commit, and confirmed with a new Packetdrill test, where the server writes data and shuts the connection down before the third ACK, from which the MPTCP options are removed. Without this patch, a FIN was sent right after this ACK, and the data was never sent:
inbound injected packet: 0.240127 . 501:501(0) ack 4103187975 win 450 outbound sniffed packet: 0.240207 F. 4103187975:4103187975(0) ack 501 win 1050 outbound sniffed packet: 1.347800 F. 4103187975:4103187975(0) ack 501 win 1050 outbound sniffed packet: 2.499829 F. 4103187975:4103187975(0) ack 501 win 1050 outbound sniffed packet: 4.739843 F. 4103187975:4103187975(0) ack 501 win 1050 server-tfo-fallback-shutdown-before-3rd-ack.pkt:27: error handling packet: Timed out waiting for packet
Fixes: d51991e2e314 ("mptcp: fix shutdown vs fallback race") Cc: user25@example.test Signed-off-by: Matthieu Baerts (NGI0) <user31@example.test> --- net/mptcp/protocol.h | 6 +++++- 1 file changed, 5 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
diff --git a/net/mptcp/protocol.h b/net/mptcp/protocol.h index 011e73d04ee6..7d226ee38315 100644 --- a/net/mptcp/protocol.h +++ b/net/mptcp/protocol.h @@ -1333,7 +1333,11 @@ static inline bool mptcp_try_fallback(struct sock *ssk, int fb_mib) msk = mptcp_sk(sk); if (!__mptcp_try_fallback(msk, fb_mib)) return false; - if (READ_ONCE(msk->snd_data_fin_enable) && !(ssk->sk_shutdown & SEND_SHUTDOWN)) { + + /* no FIN before new data: see mptcp_check_send_data_fin() */ + if (READ_ONCE(msk->snd_data_fin_enable) && + !before64(READ_ONCE(msk->snd_nxt) + 1, READ_ONCE(msk->write_seq)) && + !(ssk->sk_shutdown & SEND_SHUTDOWN)) { gfp_t saved_allocation = ssk->sk_allocation;
/* we are in a atomic (BH) scope, override ssk default for data
-- 2.55.0

entry.title: [PATCH net 5/7] mptcp: push queued data on subflows falling back at the handshake

div.pre:
With TCP Fast Open, the data written by an MPTCP server before the 3rd ACK is not sent when this ACK arrives without MPTCP options, but only when another event triggers a push, e.g. new data from the peer.
The previous commit pushes this data when the third ACK, with the MP_CAPABLE option, makes a passive TFO subflow fully established. If this ACK has no MPTCP options, e.g. because a middlebox removed them, check_fully_established() falls back to TCP, and returns before this push. The fallback case of mptcp_incoming_options(), which pushes the pending data, is only reached with the next packets.
The fix used here is to push the pending data after this fallback too. Not only for the passive TFO subflows: data can also be pending on the client side, when the first ACK from the server has no MPTCP options, e.g. if the window announced by the SYN+ACK was too small for it. Same here, this data was then only sent when another event triggered a push.
This issue has been found by an AI code review agent (Clashiko), while reviewing an earlier version of the previous commit. It has been reproduced with a new Packetdrill test, where the MPTCP options are removed from the third ACK. Without this patch, and before the earlier commit "mptcp: arm the rtx timer if a push leaves data behind", this data was not sent:
server-tfo-fallback-write-before-3rd-ack.pkt:26: error handling packet: Timed out waiting for packet
Since this earlier commit, this data is sent, but only when the MPTCP retransmission timer fires, here after one second, as the test increases its interval:
server-tfo-fallback-write-before-3rd-ack.pkt:26: error handling packet: timing error: expected outbound packet at 0.235869 sec but happened at 1.144189 sec; tolerance 0.100000 sec
The client side case has been reported by Sashiko, while reviewing an earlier version of this commit, and confirmed with another new Packetdrill test, where the client writes more data than the window of the SYN+ACK, before an ACK without MPTCP options. Without this patch:
v1_connect_fallback_pending_data.pkt:30: error handling packet: timing error: expected outbound packet at 0.251394 sec but happened at 1.195904 sec; tolerance 0.100000 sec
Two Fixes tags: the passive TFO case comes from the first commit, and the client side one from the second one.
Fixes: 36b122baf6a8 ("mptcp: add subflow_v(4,6)_send_synack()") Fixes: 6f8a612a33e4 ("mptcp: keep track of advertised windows right edge") Cc: user25@example.test Signed-off-by: Matthieu Baerts (NGI0) <user31@example.test> --- net/mptcp/options.c | 4 ++++ 1 file changed, 4 insertions(+)
diff --git a/net/mptcp/options.c b/net/mptcp/options.c index bcf3440d1901..617358ff7f99 100644 --- a/net/mptcp/options.c +++ b/net/mptcp/options.c @@ -1035,6 +1035,10 @@ static bool check_fully_established(struct mptcp_sock *msk, struct sock *ssk, MPTCP_INC_STATS(sock_net(ssk), MPTCP_MIB_FALLBACKFAILED); goto reset; } + /* this ACK will not reach the fallback path: push from here */ + mptcp_data_lock(sk); + __mptcp_check_push(sk, ssk); + mptcp_data_unlock(sk); return false; }
-- 2.55.0

entry.title: [PATCH net 4/7] mptcp: push queued data on passive TFO subflows becoming established

div.pre:
With TCP Fast Open, the data written by an MPTCP server before the 3rd ACK is not sent when this ACK arrives, but only when another event triggers a push, e.g. new data from the peer. With a request/response protocol, the client waits for the reply, which can then stay stuck.
A SYN with a valid TFO cookie creates a child socket right away, which can be accepted while its subflow is still in the SYN_RECV state. The MPTCP socket is already in the ESTABLISHED state: send() puts the data in its write queue, but this data cannot be pushed to the subflow before it is established, see __mptcp_subflow_active(). When the third ACK, with the MP_CAPABLE option, arrives, check_fully_established() marks the subflow as fully established, but nothing pushes the pending data: this ACK has no DSS option, so ack_update_msk() is not called.
The fix used here is to push the pending data when a passive TFO subflow becomes fully established. Checking subflow->is_mptfo is not enough: since commit e00b63056fb4 ("mptcp: fastopen: only mark MPTFO subflows with SYN data"), it is not set when the SYN has no data, while a child is also created in this case. syn_fastopen_child is then used instead.
This issue has been reported by a user of proxies over MPTCP: the clients put their requests in the SYN, and the replies from the targets close to the server were stuck. It has been reproduced with new Packetdrill tests, where the server writes data before the third ACK, after a SYN with and without data. Without this patch, and before the earlier commit "mptcp: arm the rtx timer if a push leaves data behind", this data was not sent:
server-tfo-write-before-3rd-ack.pkt:24: error handling packet: Timed out waiting for packet
Since this earlier commit, this data is sent, but only when the MPTCP retransmission timer fires, here after one second, as the tests increase its interval:
server-tfo-write-before-3rd-ack.pkt:24: error handling packet: timing error: expected outbound packet at 0.237174 sec but happened at 1.181857 sec; tolerance 0.100000 sec
Fixes: 36b122baf6a8 ("mptcp: add subflow_v(4,6)_send_synack()") Cc: user25@example.test Suggested-by: Petar Sakic <user40@example.test> Suggested-by: T S Rameshkumar <user41@example.test> Reported-by: Petar Sakic <user40@example.test> Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/mptcp/user42@example.test/ Signed-off-by: Matthieu Baerts (NGI0) <user31@example.test> --- net/mptcp/options.c | 2 ++ 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+)

mptcp_data_lock(sk); __mptcp_subflow_fully_established(msk, subflow, mp_opt); + if (tcp_sk(ssk)->syn_fastopen_child) + __mptcp_check_push(sk, ssk); mptcp_data_unlock(sk);

entry.title: [PATCH net 2/7] mptcp: push pending data after a sendmsg copy fault

div.pre:
From: Quanye Yang <user45@example.test>
mptcp_sendmsg() copies into the msk write queue first, then __mptcp_push_pending() on the success path. tcp_sendmsg_locked() does the opposite: its do_error path jumps to out, and out calls tcp_push() when copied > 0.
A later iovec fault (copy_from_iter / -EFAULT) after a successful iteration therefore returns the partial byte count but leaves the already-queued dfrag on rtx_queue. No subflow packet is sent, no retransmission timer is armed, and DATA_FIN stays blocked on first_pending.
Push in do_error when copied is already non-zero. Do not move the push to out: copied is a size_t, and sk_stream_error() stores a negative errno there.
The issue was spot by Sashiko, but easy to reproduce with Packetdrill:
writev(4, [{..., 32728}, {NULL, 4096}], 2) = 32728
Fixes: 69800e516e96 ("mptcp: propagate fastclose error") Cc: user25@example.test Closes: https://github.com/multipath-tcp/mptcp_net-next/issues/640 Signed-off-by: Quanye Yang <user45@example.test> Reviewed-by: Matthieu Baerts (NGI0) <user31@example.test> Signed-off-by: Matthieu Baerts (NGI0) <user31@example.test> --- net/mptcp/protocol.c | 4 +++- 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
diff --git a/net/mptcp/protocol.c b/net/mptcp/protocol.c index 8968db58083e..b67096ee131b 100644 --- a/net/mptcp/protocol.c +++ b/net/mptcp/protocol.c @@ -2130,8 +2130,10 @@ static int mptcp_sendmsg(struct sock *sk, struct msghdr *msg, size_t len) return copied;
do_error: - if (copied) + if (copied) { + __mptcp_push_pending(sk, msg->msg_flags); goto out; + }
copied = sk_stream_error(sk, msg->msg_flags, ret); goto out;
-- 2.55.0

entry.title: [PATCH] gfs2: Fix NULL pointer dereference in gfs2_seek_data/gfs2_seek_hole
[PATCH net 1/7] mptcp: do not use a raised snd_wnd for the send window

div.pre:
ack_update_msk() sets the right edge of the MPTCP send window from the DATA_ACK and tcp_sk(ssk)->snd_wnd, but this is not always what the peer announced: mptcp_check_allowed_size() raises it to window_end - data_seq, so that TCP lets through what the MPTCP-level window allows.
That is fine for new data. For data sent again, data_seq can be below snd_una, and snd_wnd ends up too large by the difference. TCP only overwrites it when an ACK moves things forward on this subflow, see tcp_may_update_window(). If a DATA_ACK moved by another subflow comes in on this subflow before that, wnd_end goes past what the peer offered. It only moves forward, so it stays there.
The sender then transmits data beyond the peer's window: the peer drops it (MPTCP_MIB_NODSSWINDOW) after TCP acked it, and only an MPTCP-level retransmission can recover it, which raises snd_wnd again. The connection can then stay stuck at a low rate for several seconds, with nothing in flight on any subflow.
This raise has been added by commit b713d0067574 ("mptcp: really share subflow snd_wnd"), but snd_wnd could already be too large before: when nothing moves at the TCP level, tcp_may_update_window() ignores a lower non-zero window, while the peer can announce one with a DATA_ACK that moved, keeping the same right edge.
Use the window announced in the packet carrying the DATA_ACK instead.
In my case with BBR, a small TCP rmem, and a second path with a much higher latency, a lower throughput and some losses, this small change can double the throughput in the worst cases.
The issue has been reproduced with a new Packetdrill test, on a single subflow: the data is acked by TCP, then by MPTCP with a lower window, keeping the same right edge. Without this patch, the 2000 bytes written next were sent, instead of the 1280 bytes up to this right edge:
dss_dack_window_server.pkt:23: error handling packet: live packet payload: expected 1280 bytes vs actual 2000 bytes
Fixes: 6f8a612a33e4 ("mptcp: keep track of advertised windows right edge") Cc: user25@example.test Signed-off-by: Matthieu Baerts (NGI0) <user31@example.test> --- net/mptcp/options.c | 11 +++++++++-- 1 file changed, 9 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)
diff --git a/net/mptcp/options.c b/net/mptcp/options.c index 02e785a14b8a..a1e65309171e 100644 --- a/net/mptcp/options.c +++ b/net/mptcp/options.c @@ -1120,9 +1120,11 @@ static void rwin_update(struct mptcp_sock *msk, struct sock *ssk,
static void ack_update_msk(struct mptcp_sock *msk, struct sock *ssk, + const struct sk_buff *skb, struct mptcp_options_received *mp_opt) { u64 new_wnd_end, new_snd_una, old_snd_una; + u32 win = ntohs(tcp_hdr(skb)->window); struct sock *sk = (struct sock *)msk; u64 snd_nxt;
@@ -1143,7 +1145,12 @@ static void ack_update_msk(struct mptcp_sock *msk, after64(new_snd_una, snd_nxt))) new_snd_una = old_snd_una;
- new_wnd_end = new_snd_una + tcp_sk(ssk)->snd_wnd; + /* What the peer announced: tcp_sk(ssk)->snd_wnd can be larger, see + * mptcp_check_allowed_size(), and is not always updated. + */ + if (likely(!tcp_hdr(skb)->syn))

--
selftests: net: test restricted on-link fallback
This patch updates the IPv4 cases in fcnal-test.sh to match the new on-link fallback behaviour. The fallback is no longer taken when the FIB lookup hits an unreachable, blackhole or prohibit route or rule. It changes the expected return codes, adds a route miss variant and an unreachable rule case, and enables the device bind cases that were previously commented out.
> diff --git a/tools/testing/selftests/net/fcnal-test.sh b/tools/testing/selftests/net/fcnal-test.sh > index a50609535fedc..9722d7dcad085 100755 > --- a/tools/testing/selftests/net/fcnal-test.sh > +++ b/tools/testing/selftests/net/fcnal-test.sh
[ ... ]
> @@ -643,10 +656,14 @@ ipv4_ping_novrf() > run_cmd ping -c1 -w1 ${a} > log_test_addr ${a} $? 2 "ping out, blocked by rule" > > - # NOTE: ipv4 actually allows the lookup to fail and yet still create > - # a viable rtable if the oif (e.g., bind to device) is set, so this > - # case succeeds despite the rule > - # run_cmd ping -c1 -w1 -I ${NSA_DEV} ${a} > + log_start > + setup_cmd ip rule add pref 49 to ${NSB_LO_IP} unreachable > + log_test_addr ${a} $? 2 "ping out, blocked by unreachable rule"
[Severity: Medium] Is a ping missing here? Nothing runs between the rule add and log_test_addr, so $? is the exit status of setup_cmd.
setup_cmd() exits the whole script if the command fails:
setup_cmd() { ... run_cmd ${cmd} rc=$? if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then ... exit $rc fi }
So when it returns here, $? is always 0. log_test_addr() then compares 0 against the expected value of 2. That means this case reports FAIL on every run, and no packet is ever sent while the pref 49 unreachable rule is installed.
The commit message says this case will "demonstrate ping fails as expected with an unreachable rule" and that it "ensures FIB_LOOKUP_REPORT_MISS does not break this behavior". As written, the case checks neither.
Would adding run_cmd ping -c1 -w1 ${a} before log_test_addr fix this? At this point a is still ${NSB_LO_IP}.
> + setup_cmd ip rule del pref 49 to ${NSB_LO_IP} unreachable > + > + log_start > + run_cmd ping -c1 -w1 -I ${NSA_DEV} ${a} > + log_test_addr ${a} $? 2 "ping out, device bind, blocked by rule"
[Severity: Low] Even with the ping added, can the unreachable rule case catch a FIB_LOOKUP_REPORT_MISS regression without a device bind?
In ip_route_output_key_hash_rcu(), the on-link fallback is only taken when oif is set and err == -ESRCH. In every other case a miss is mapped back:
err = err == -ESRCH ? -ENETUNREACH : err;

entry.title: Re: [PATCH net-next v4 2/4] ipv4: restrict on-link fallback to lookup misses

div.pre:
Thank you for your contribution! Sashiko AI review found more severe issue(s) in other patches of this series. This mail is only an FYI, in case you want to address the nit picks below when you respin.
Low priority / nit picks for your consideration:
- [Low] The commit "ipv4: restrict on-link fallback to lookup misses" is written up as a bug fix with security impact: "unprivileged Android…
--
ipv4: restrict on-link fallback to lookup misses
This patch changes ip_route_output_key_hash_rcu() so that, for non-vrf unicast with an oif set, the on-link fallback happens only when fib_lookup() reports a lookup miss (-ESRCH via FIB_LOOKUP_REPORT_MISS). Before, it happened for any lookup error. Blackhole, prohibit and unreachable routes and rules are now honored for oif-bound sends, and -ESRCH is mapped back to -ENETUNREACH on the error path.
> A specific example of this being a problem is within Android, where the > VPN "kill switch" is implemented with prohibit rules. Any process that > can set flowi4_oif (SO_BINDTODEVICE, IP_UNICAST_IF, IP_PKTINFO, etc.) is > able to utilize this fallback, meaning unprivileged Android apps can > trivially bypass the VPN. This is particularly bad on cellular networks, > where ARP is often not needed.
[ ... ]
> Signed-off-by: Liam Smith <user57@example.test>
[Severity: Low] This isn't a code bug, but should the commit carry a Fixes: tag?
The message describes this as a fix for a VPN bypass. The trailer block only has Signed-off-by. Documentation/process/maintainer-netdev.rst says:
"for fixes the Fixes: tag is required, regardless of the tree"
In ip_route_output_key_hash_rcu(), falling back to on-link for any fib_lookup() error goes back to:
1da177e4c3f4 ("Linux-2.6.12-rc2")
The baseline form of the condition this patch changes:
(ipv4_is_multicast(fl4->daddr) || !fl4->flowi4_l3mdev)
comes from:
40867d74c374 ("net: Add l3mdev index to flow struct and avoid oif reset for port devices")
Could one of these be named in a Fixes: tag? That would make it clear whether this change is meant for stable. It also changes what oif-bound sockets see when they hit reject routes or rules: those sends now return an error instead of going out on-link.
-- Sashiko AI review · https://netdev-ai.bots.linux.dev/sashiko/#/patchset/20261115215640.18728-1-liamsmith827%40grapheneos.org
